newsitem.title: USA: Trade partner growth seen as vital as dollar level.
newsitem.headline: Trade partner growth seen as vital as dollar level.

text.p: Growth in the economies of U.S. trading partners seemed to be offsetting the export dampening effects of recent dollar strength, Commerce Department economist Lee Price said Friday.
"Analysis of 20, 30 years of trade data suggests that exchange rates matter but immediate growth and relative growth rates matter just as much," Price told Reuters Financial Television.

"I think the strength that we've seen in our exports suggests there is underlying strength in the economies and domestic demand in our trading partners that wasn't there a year ago that seems to be offsetting whatever fears about the dollar people had," he said.
